original: Introduction In today's rapidly evolving research landscape, label noise plays a crucial role in the reliability of supervised learning. Moreover, it is important to note that modern datasets often contain between 8% and 38% mislabelled examples [1], [2]. Furthermore, existing methods leverage a myriad of heuristics that may potentially fail when the noise is structured. Additionally, these approaches delve into the intricate relationships between features and labels without a principled account of uncertainty. In this paper, we propose a deterministic filtering framework that achieves robust performance across five benchmarks. The framework utilizes a small ensemble of linear models, which are trained on disjoint folds of the data. We demonstrate that the method reduces the error rate from 14.2% to 9.7% on CIFAR-10N while requiring only 3 GPU-hours. It is worth noting that the method does not require clean validation labels. However, it cannot recover labels that are systematically flipped by annotators. Related Work

Moreover, it is important to note that modern datasets often contain between 8% and 38% mislabelled examples [1], [2]. Furthermore, existing methods leverage a myriad of heuristics that may potentially fail when the noise is structured. Additionally, these approaches delve into the intricate relationships between features and labels without a principled account of uncertainty. In this paper, we propose a deterministic filtering framework that achieves robust performance across five benchmarks. The framework utilizes a small ensemble of linear models, which are trained on disjoint folds of the data. We demonstrate that the method reduces the error rate from 14.2% to 9.7% on CIFAR-10N while requiring only 3 GPU-hours. It is worth noting that the method does not require clean validation labels. However, it cannot recover labels that are systematically flipped by annotators. Related Work

original: Introduction In today's rapidly evolving research landscape, label noise plays a crucial role in the reliability of supervised learning. Moreover, it is important to note that modern datasets often contain between 8% and 38% mislabelled examples [1], [2]. Furthermore, existing methods leverage a myriad of heuristics that may potentially fail when the noise is structured. Additionally, these approaches delve into the intricate relationships between features and labels without a principled account of uncertainty. In this paper, we propose a deterministic filtering framework that achieves robust performance across five benchmarks. The framework utilizes a small ensemble of linear models, which are trained on disjoint folds of the data. We demonstrate that the method reduces the error rate from 14.2% to 9.7% on CIFAR-10N while requiring only 3 GPU-hours. It is worth noting that the method does not require clean validation labels. However, it cannot recover labels that are systematically flipped by annotators. Related Work

original: Modern techniques of image restoration have become more inclined towards the use of GANs together with diffusion models. The use of DCGAN [radford2015dcgan] and StyleGAN [karras2019stylegan] have led to the development of strong convolutional and style-based generator functions that provide realistic samples. At the same time, WGAN-GP [gulrajani2017wgangp], which is based on Wasserstein critic and gradient-norm regularizer, almost eliminates mode collapsing. On the contrary, diffusion models, which were first proposed by Sohl-Dickstein et al. [sohl2015deep] and later described theoretically by Ho et al. [ho2020ddpm] as denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM), offer stable training and good iterative performance. Song et al. [song2020ddim] have developed DDIM or denoising diffusion implicit models for efficient inference, using the cosine noise schedule from Nichol and Dhariwal [nichol2021improved]. In case of image-to-image translation and low-level restoration tasks, SR3 [saharia2022sr3] and Palette [saharia2022palette] use conditional diffusion model by channel-wise concatenation of the degraded conditioning input. In addition, SDEdit [meng2021sdedit] shows that noisying only part of the corrupted input at an intermediate time step is more effective compared to starting with pure Gaussian noise, which we adopted for our task as well.

At the same time, WGAN-GP [gulrajani2017wgangp], which is based on Wasserstein critic and gradient-norm regularizer, nearly eliminates mode collapsing. On the contrary, diffusion models, which were first proposed by Sohl-Dickstein et al. [sohl2015deep] and later described theoretically by Ho et al. In case of image-to-image translation and low-level restoration tasks, SR3 [saharia2022sr3] and Palette [saharia2022palette] employ conditional diffusion model by channel-wise concatenation of the degraded conditioning input. Beyond this, SDEdit [meng2021sdedit] demonstrates that noisying only part of the corrupted input at an intermediate time step is more effective relative to beginning with pure Gaussian noise, which we adopted for our task as well.

original: Yet, understanding videos of longer duration is computationally challenging because visual context grows with the number and resolution of sampled frames. There are several techniques used to minimize the cost of representing long videos. For instance, LLaMA-VID uses compressed visual representations that lower the visual tokens [li2023llamavid]. On the other hand, MovieChat utilizes sparse memory that preserves temporally scattered information from long videos [song2024moviechat]. Some recent research is done in the field of structured and adaptive visual token reduction [ju2026forestprune, xu2026score]. Examples of benchmarking include LongVideoBench and Video-MME demonstrate the difficulty of retrieval, temporal reasoning, and multimodal understanding as video context becomes longer and more diverse [wu2024longvideobench, fu2025videomme]. original: Introduction In today's rapidly evolving research landscape, label noise plays a crucial role in the reliability of supervised learning. Moreover, it is important to note that modern datasets often contain between 8% and 38% mislabelled examples [1], [2]. Furthermore, existing methods leverage a myriad of heuristics that may potentially fail when the noise is structured. Additionally, these approaches delve into the intricate relationships between features and labels without a principled account of uncertainty. In this paper, we propose a deterministic filtering framework that achieves robust performance across five benchmarks. The framework utilizes a small ensemble of linear models, which are trained on disjoint folds of the data. We demonstrate that the method reduces the error rate from 14.2% to 9.7% on CIFAR-10N while requiring only 3 GPU-hours. It is worth noting that the method does not require clean validation labels. However, it cannot recover labels that are systematically flipped by annotators. Related Work
rewritten: Introduction In today's quickly evolving research landscape, label noise is crucial for the reliability of supervised learning. Moreover, modern datasets frequently contain between 8% and 38% mislabelled instances [1], [2]. Existing methods leverage many heuristics that may fail when the noise is structured. These approaches examine the complex relationships between features and labels without a principled account of uncertainty. We propose a deterministic filtering framework that achieves robust performance across five benchmarks in this paper. The framework uses a small ensemble of linear models, which are trained on disjoint folds of the data. We show that the method lowers the error rate from 14.2% to 9.7% on CIFAR-10N while needing only 3 GPU-hours. The method does not need clean validation labels. That said, it cannot recover labels that are methodically flipped by annotators. Related Work

original: Introduction In today's rapidly evolving research landscape, label noise plays a crucial role in the reliability of supervised learning. Moreover, it is important to note that modern datasets often contain between 8% and 38% mislabelled examples [1], [2]. Furthermore, existing methods leverage a myriad of heuristics that may potentially fail when the noise is structured. Additionally, these approaches delve into the intricate relationships between features and labels without a principled account of uncertainty. In this paper, we propose a deterministic filtering framework that achieves robust performance across five benchmarks. The framework utilizes a small ensemble of linear models, which are trained on disjoint folds of the data. We demonstrate that the method reduces the error rate from 14.2% to 9.7% on CIFAR-10N while requiring only 3 GPU-hours. It is worth noting that the method does not require clean validation labels. However, it cannot recover labels that are systematically flipped by annotators. Related Work

original: Abstract CANTOR is a causal audio-language framework designed to move singing assessment from simple error detection toward theory-grounded and explainable diagnosis. This report presents the evolution of the project from its initial proposal through data harmonization, model selection, and the final acoustic-reasoning pipeline. Eight heterogeneous singing corpora are harmonized into a common representation hosted on Kaggle, preserving source provenance and distinguishing original annotations from derived features. This document outlines the systematic integration of a Temporal Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) head atop a foundational HuBERT encoder for acoustic feature extraction, and the subsequent instruction-tuning of Llama-3 for interpretable vocal reasoning. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) on the CANTOR_v2_Reasoned_Dataset.csv validates the modality coverage and schema integrity necessary for causal diagnostics. Keywords: Singing Voice Assessment; Audio-Language Models; Explainable AI; Multimodal Learning; Dataset Harmonization; HuBERT; Convolutional Neural Networks.

original: Introduction In today's rapidly evolving research landscape, label noise plays a crucial role in the reliability of supervised learning. Moreover, it is important to note that modern datasets often contain between 8% and 38% mislabelled examples [1], [2]. Furthermore, existing methods leverage a myriad of heuristics that may potentially fail when the noise is structured. Additionally, these approaches delve into the intricate relationships between features and labels without a principled account of uncertainty. In this paper, we propose a deterministic filtering framework that achieves robust performance across five benchmarks. The framework utilizes a small ensemble of linear models, which are trained on disjoint folds of the data. We demonstrate that the method reduces the error rate from 14.2% to 9.7% on CIFAR-10N while requiring only 3 GPU-hours. It is worth noting that the method does not require clean validation labels. However, it cannot recover labels that are systematically flipped by annotators. Related Work
rewritten: Introduction In today's quickly evolving research landscape, label noise is crucial for the reliability of supervised learning. Moreover, modern datasets frequently contain between 8% and 38% mislabelled instances [1], [2]. Existing methods leverage a myriad of heuristics that may fail when the noise is structured. These approaches examine the complex relationships between features and labels without a principled account of uncertainty. We propose a deterministic filtering framework that achieves robust performance across five benchmarks in this paper. The framework uses a small ensemble of linear models, which are trained on disjoint folds of the data. We show that the method lowers the error rate from 14.2% to 9.7% on CIFAR-10N while needing only 3 GPU-hours. The method does not need clean validation labels. That said, it cannot recover labels that are methodically flipped by annotators. Related Work
